div.head: Abt 76
div.ab: Gif man widuwan unagne genimeþ, II gelde seo mund sy.
Gif man widuwan unagne genimeþ, II gelde seo mund sy.
Gif man widuwan unagne genimeþ, II gelde seo mund sy.
Wenn jemand eine Wittwe, die nicht sein eigen ist, [sondern unter Vormundschaft eines Dritten,] entführt, sei [er diesem jene Summe für Bruch der] Schutzgewalt zwiefach [schuldig].
If someone carries off a widow who is not his own [but under the guardianship of a third party], let [him owe that party the sum for breach of the] protective authority twofold.
If a man takes a widow who does not [of right] belong to him, double the value of the mund shall be paid.
If a man takes a widow who does not belong to him, the [penalty for breach of the] guardianship is to be doubled.
If a person takes a widow who does not belong to him, the [payment for violation of] protection shall be 2[-fold] as compensation.

note.note: One footnote serves three places on p. 7: Abt 74, 76 and 77.

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Eheschliessung 2f. — ‘In alterius (mundo), alienam, non suam sagen Festlandsgermanen; Lex Fris. 88; Rothari 198; Loening Gesch. Dt. Kirchenr. II 606. Der Ggs. liegt vor, wenn der Vormund selbst die Witwe heiratet, was zu erzwingen die Langobarden verbieten; Wilda 842

Cf. Gl Eheschliessung 2f. — The continental Germanic peoples say ‘In alterius (mundo), alienam, non suam; Lex Fris. 88; Rothari 198; Loening Gesch. Dt. Kirchenr. II 606. The opposite case is where the guardian himself marries the widow, which the Lombards forbid him to force; Wilda 842
‘Doppelt Wittum’ verstehen Schröder (Gesch. ehel. Güterr. I 14) und Yonge Essays in Ags. law 166
Schröder (Gesch. ehel. Güterr. I 14) and Yonge Essays in Ags. law 166 take it as ‘double dower’
